name: Larust Blade
comment: Two different techniques for two different needs, both confirmed directly against the real vscode-textmate engine, not assumed: (1) this language's own custom TAGS (<Image>/<wire:>/<resource:>) are real top-level patterns, listed BEFORE text.html.derivative, so they win the tie at a fresh '<' - an injection can't do this, since by the time content is inside the base grammar's own meta.tag state, an injection targeting that state loses to whatever already-active rule the base grammar is running (confirmed directly: tried <Image> as an injection first, and the base grammar's own generic <tagname> pattern claimed it instead, silently swallowing the whole :dynamic= attribute as unscoped text). (2) everything that needs to interrupt content the base grammar already owns mid-span (plain text between tags, ordinary attribute values) - {{ }}/{!! !!}/comments/directives/@globals - follows the same proven structure the already-installed onecentlin.laravel-blade extension uses for its own text.html.php.blade (confirmed by reading its real, shipped grammar): injected into text.html.derivative rather than listed as flat top-level siblings, since a flat sibling never gets a chance to fire once the included grammar's own rules have already claimed a span.

L:(text.html.larust-blade meta.tag - (co.comment: Two reasons this needs L: priority inside meta.tag, not just the base grammar's own handling: (1) {{ }}/{!! !!} can appear inside an *ordinary* HTML tag's own attribute values (e.g. <div class="{{ expr }}">), which the base grammar is still actively parsing when they do. (2) attribute VALUES getting a real, distinct string scope must never depend on whatever text.html.derivative happens to do for an *ordinary* (non-custom) tag's own attributes - reported directly, from a real screenshot: attribute values and plain element text content were rendering as the exact same color, meaning they weren't being told apart at all. #attribute-literal here guarantees every attr="value"/attr='value' pair gets this grammar's own explicit string.quoted scope, regardless of tag.

rust-fallback.comment: Basic string/number/keyword highlighting for every { }} / {!! !!} / :attr="..." / @globals region, used alongside source.rust (not instead of it) so these regions still render reasonably even when no separate Rust grammar is registered - confirmed directly: a rule whose own patterns list is *only* an unresolvable {"include": "source.rust"} goes completely inert in vscode-textmate (the whole begin/end region fails to tokenize at all, not just the inner Rust-specific coloring), tested against the real vscode-textmate/vscode-oniguruma engine, not assumed from the spec alone.

literal-string-single.comment: This templating language's own directive-argument strings are conventionally single-quoted (@extends('layouts.app'), @wire('search-box'), @section('content') - confirmed from real usage throughout this repo) - but real Rust has no single-quoted STRING syntax at all; a single quote there means a char literal ('a') or a lifetime ('static, no closing quote). Reported directly, via VS Code's own scope inspector: source.rust was misinterpreting 'layouts.app' as a lifetime ('layouts, stopping at the period since identifiers can't contain one), leaving '.app' as a trailing, completely unscoped mess - a visibly broken, half-colored result, not just a missed opportunity for richer coloring. Listed BEFORE source.rust everywhere both appear, so a real single-quoted span is claimed atomically as a string before the lifetime-matching ever gets a chance to misfire on its opening quote. Only matches a span with a genuine closing quote, so an actual Rust lifetime ('static, no closing quote) is correctly left untouched - the one real Rust construct this could have collided with.
literal-string-single.name: string.quoted.single.larust-blade

directive.comment: Split into two scopes, not one uniform keyword.control, mirroring the real distinction onecentlin.laravel-blade's own grammar makes (confirmed by reading it directly): structural block-pair directives (if/foreach/section/... and their own @end* closers) are genuinely control-flow, kept as keyword.control; simple, non-block directives (extends/yield/csrf/...) get their own support.function scope instead, the same family most themes already color distinctly from control-flow keywords - matching onecentlin's own split between its block-keyword list and its separate entity.name.function.blade catch-all. Two real regex capture groups, not a nested 'patterns' re-scan - a plain match rule's own 'patterns' field is a no-op; sub-tokenizing a single match requires capture groups + 'captures', confirmed directly after an earlier draft of this rule silently did nothing.
